items.name: JPG, WebP and AVIF
items.text: Lowers the quality to the point where the difference stops being perceptible.

items.name: PNG
items.text: Reduces the color palette when the difference is not noticeable. In high quality it keeps every pixel.

items.name: GIF
items.text: Keeps the animation and reduces the weight of the file.

items.name: SVG
items.text: Removes scripts and unnecessary code, without changing its appearance.

items.name: ZIP
items.text: It is read in parts, so even a very large zip is explored immediately.

items.name: Videos and others
items.text: They are not processed: you are told which ones were left out.

steps.title: Reading
steps.text: The image is opened in the browser and checked for what it really is: its content, its dimensions and its format.

steps.title: Measurement
steps.text: It is compressed at several quality levels and each result is compared with the original, in brightness and in color.

steps.title: Selection
steps.text: The lightest version that passes the threshold of the chosen level is kept. If none weighs less, the original is kept.

steps.title: Verification
steps.text: Before the result is delivered, it is measured on the full image and not only on a sample.

band.title: A thousand images in a single browser tab.
band.text: The work is split across the cores of the processor and zips are read in parts, without loading them whole into memory. That is why a large zip is explored immediately.

facts.label: to read a zip of 1000 images

items.title: Content verification
items.text: Every file is identified by its content and not by its extension. A .jpg file that actually contains text is rejected.

items.title: Protection against malicious zips
items.text: Paths that try to leave the destination folder, password-protected entries and files that, once unpacked, far exceed the size they declare are rejected.

items.title: SVGs without scripts
items.text: Scripts and external links are removed from SVG files, and they are only shown as images, never as pages.

items.title: Protection of personal data
items.text: JPG and PNG files lose their hidden data, such as the camera model and the location, unless it is requested to keep it.

items.a: Not visibly, at the recommended level. Squeezo compresses each image at several quality levels, compares each result with the original in brightness and in color, and only accepts the version whose difference cannot be seen at a glance. If you need maximum fidelity, the "High quality" level demands differences that are imperceptible even when zooming in, in exchange for a smaller weight reduction.

items.q: Do the dimensions of the image change?
items.a: No. Width and height stay the same, unless you turn on the dimension limit in the settings. In that case only the images that exceed the chosen limit are reduced, and their proportions are kept.

items.q: How much is the weight reduced?
items.a: It depends on each image. In tests with photographs, the recommended level reduced the weight by roughly 55% to 80%, and by more than 90% in PNG screenshots. Images that were already well optimized are left unchanged and you are told so.

JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, GIF (animated too), SVG and BMP. TIFF and HEIC are processed only in browsers that can read them. GIF and SVG files always keep their format, and animated PNG, WebP or AVIF images are left unchanged so the animation is not lost.

items.q: What happens to videos and other files inside a zip?
items.a: They are skipped, and you are told how many there were and of what kind. Executables are dropped for safety. Squeezo only compresses images.
Up to 1000 images per zip and up to 50 megapixels per image are accepted. These limits protect the memory of the browser and prevent the device from being overloaded.

items.q: Are my files sent to any server?
items.a: No. All processing takes place in your own browser. No file is sent to a server and no account is needed. The only thing that may be sent, and only if you allow it in the cookie preferences, is the number of images reduced when a compression finishes, for the global counter on the About page.

items.q: What happens if I reload the page or close the tab?
items.a: It depends on the cookie preferences. If you allow the working session to be saved, your progress is kept and, when you return, it is restored exactly as it was, even if a compression was halfway through, which resumes automatically. If you do not allow it, the files and the results are lost when the page is reloaded. The "Clear" button deletes the saved data in any case.

items.q: Are the camera data and the location kept?
items.a: By default they are removed from JPG and PNG files. If you need to keep them, you can turn that option on in the compression settings.

p: Squeezo works entirely in the browser. Images, folders and zip files are never sent to a server, and no registration or personal data is needed to use the tool.
This principle comes down to three commitments:

ul: the user's files do not leave their device;
there are no accounts, tracking cookies or analytics;
the only data that reaches a server is what is strictly necessary for the global counter, and it is detailed below.

p: To make the distinction clear, this is the data according to how it is handled:

p.sub: Processed only on the user's device

ul: the images, folders and zip files that are added;
the results of the compression;
the preferences and settings chosen.
the number of images compressed when each compression finishes;
the technical data of each visit that the hosting provider records.
names, email addresses or any other data that identifies the user;
the content, the names or the properties of the files;
the location or data about the device.

p: Files are read and processed on the user's device, using the resources of its own processor. Squeezo receives no copy of them, does not analyze them remotely and does not share them with third parties.
This includes the files inside a zip: they are read in parts in the browser itself and are never transmitted.
Squeezo uses the browser's own storage so that work is not lost when the page is reloaded. What is saved depends on the permissions the person grants in the cookie preferences:

ul: always, the language, the theme and the decision about cookies, in local storage;
only with permission, the compression settings, in local storage;
only with permission, the working session, that is, the files added and the results, in the browser's database (IndexedDB).

p: This data does not leave the device, is not tied to any identity and is not shared with any server.

sections.h: How to delete the saved data
p: The user can delete what Squeezo saves in their browser at any time, in four ways:

ol: withdrawing the permissions on the cookie page, which immediately deletes the data tied to each one;
pressing the "Clear" button in the file list, which deletes the working session;
deleting the site data from the browser settings, which also deletes the preferences;
using a private or incognito window, where nothing is kept once it is closed.

p: After deletion, the tool returns to its initial state.

Squeezo shows on the About page the total number of images compressed by everyone who uses it. To keep that figure, and only if the user allows it in the cookie preferences, the browser sends a single piece of data to a server when a compression finishes: the number of images reduced.

p.sub: What is sent and what is stored

ul: only a whole number is sent;
only the accumulated total is stored, unrelated to any person or session;
no files, names, content or identifiers are sent.

p: To prevent the figure from being falsified, the submissions that a single address can make in one minute are limited. For that purpose, the IP address is converted into a short fingerprint that is kept for one minute and then deleted.
The counter is stored on Upstash, a database service used through Vercel.
There are no user accounts, tracking cookies, analytics or advertising. Squeezo does not collect names, email addresses or any other data that identifies the user.
Since no personal data is processed, there are no profiles, no statistics are drawn up per person and no automated decisions are made.
Squeezo installs no tracking or advertising cookies. The only storage technologies it uses are local storage and the browser's database, and only for the operation described in this policy.

The person decides which of them are turned on through the notice shown on the first visit and the cookie policy page, where the decision can be changed at any time. None of them is used to identify or follow the user across sites.
Photographs often include hidden data, known as metadata, which can reveal personal information. Among it:

ul: the model of the camera or phone;
the date and time the photo was taken;
the location where it was taken;
the color profile and other technical data.

p: When a JPG or a PNG is compressed, that data is removed, unless the user turns on the option to keep it, in which case the location may still be included. If an image cannot be reduced, it is returned unchanged and with its original metadata.

The site is hosted on Vercel, which may log technical data about each visit, such as the IP address, the date and the type of browser, under its own privacy policy. Those logs do not include the images or their content.
This project has no access to those logs for the purpose of tracking people.
Squeezo includes no third-party scripts, fonts or resources: everything is served from the site itself. The external services involved are:

ul: Vercel, for hosting the site and the counter function;
Upstash, for storing the counter total;
GitHub, where the source code is published.

p: The links to the repository on GitHub and to the libraries used lead to external sites, which are governed by their own privacy policies.
Squeezo examines the real content of every file, never runs anything that is added, rejects zips that pose a risk and removes scripts from SVG files.

The site is served with a restrictive content security policy, which prevents resources from other origins from loading and limits connections to its own domain. This reduces the possibility of foreign scripts being injected.
How long data is kept depends on each item:

ul: files and results saved in the browser remain until the user deletes them;
preferences remain until the site data is deleted;
the short fingerprint of the IP address is deleted after one minute;
the counter total is kept for as long as the service is active, and it is not tied to any person.

p: Since Squeezo does not store personal data on its servers, there is no information to access, correct or delete there. The user keeps full control over what is saved in their own browser, and can delete it whenever they want, as explained above.
For the technical logs kept by the hosting provider, rights can be exercised under that provider's privacy policy.
Squeezo does not collect personal data from anyone, including minors, and it is not aimed at a specific audience. Use by minors should be supervised by whoever has legal responsibility for them.

Any change to the data sent to a server will be reflected here before it is applied.

ul: the website and its information pages;

p: If the service is used on behalf of an organization, the person using it states that they have the authority to accept these terms on its behalf.

Squeezo is a free, open source tool that reduces the weight of images, folders and zip files directly in the user's browser. It requires no registration or user account, and it includes no paid features.

ul: compression of JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, GIF, SVG and BMP images, keeping the original dimensions unless the user chooses otherwise;
reading of folders and zip files, with a view of their contents before compressing;
a comparison between the original and the compressed image;
download of the results individually or in a zip file.
storage of files on servers or backups of the user's work;
accounts, history across devices or synchronization;
editing, cropping or processing of videos or of files that are not images.

p: The operation of Squeezo depends on the capabilities of the browser and the device it is used on. Proper use requires:

ul: an up-to-date browser with JavaScript, WebAssembly and IndexedDB enabled;
enough available memory for the size and number of images being processed;
free space on the device to save the results.

p: Some formats, such as TIFF and HEIC, can only be processed in browsers that support them. On a device with limited resources, processing large batches may be slow or may be interrupted.
The tool must be used only with images over which the user has the right of use. Personal, educational, professional and commercial use is allowed, as long as these terms are respected.
The following is forbidden:

ul: processing unlawful content or content that infringes the rights of third parties;
attempting to alter the operation of the service, bypass its limits or overload its resources;
sending automated or mass requests to the global counter in order to falsify the figure;
using the service for purposes that harm other people.

p: Failure to follow these rules may lead to access to the service being restricted.
Files remain the property of their owner. Squeezo does not receive them, does not store them on servers and does not share them, because all processing takes place in the browser itself.

The tool never modifies the originals: it creates compressed copies that are downloaded separately. When an image cannot be reduced without a noticeable loss, it is returned unchanged and this is indicated in the list.
The user states that they have the right to process the files they add and takes responsibility for their content.
Squeezo offers four levels, which can be changed in the settings before compressing:

ul: Recommended: seeks the greatest weight reduction without the change being visible at a glance. It is the default level.
High quality: requires differences that are imperceptible even when the image is enlarged, in exchange for a smaller reduction.
Maximum compression: prioritizes the lowest possible weight, and changes may be noticeable when the image is enlarged.
Custom: allows the quality of each image to be set manually.

p: The user can also choose the output format, limit the maximum dimensions and decide whether the metadata of JPG files is kept. GIF and SVG files always keep their format. The options chosen are the user's responsibility, and they can be reset at any time.

Squeezo aims for the difference between the original and the compressed image not to be perceptible at a glance, and it verifies each result before accepting it. However, no lossy compression guarantees a result identical to the original, and the effect may vary depending on the image and the chosen level.
Higher compression levels, format conversion and dimension reduction may produce visible differences. To check, it is recommended to:

ol: review the results with the comparison view before downloading them;
use the High quality level for images that will be printed or enlarged;

p: Images that were already highly optimized are left unchanged, so the weight of the resulting image never exceeds that of the original.

The results can be downloaded individually or in a single zip file. The zip respects the order of entry and the folder structure of the files added, and it keeps the modification date and time of each file.

In browsers that allow it, the zip can be saved directly to the location the user chooses. In the others, it is downloaded through the browser's download manager. Files downloaded one by one do not keep the original modification date, because the browser does not allow it.
Once downloaded, the files are under the exclusive control of the user, who is responsible for keeping them.

To avoid losing progress, and provided the user allows it in the cookie preferences, the working session is saved in the browser storage, including the files added and the results obtained. That data stays on the device until the permission is withdrawn, "Clear" is pressed or the site data is deleted from the browser settings.

On shared or public devices it is recommended not to grant that permission or to clear the session when finished, since anyone with access to the same browser profile could see the saved files. The storage is local: it is not synchronized with other devices or with any server.
To protect the operation of the browser, the following limits apply:

ul: up to 1000 images per zip and per load;
up to 50 megapixels per image;
up to 768 MB per file once decompressed;
up to 100,000 entries read from the directory of a zip;
up to 5 minutes of processing per image; if exceeded, it is discarded.

p: Files that are not images, password-protected files, executables and files that pose a security risk are excluded from processing, and the list of what was left out is shown to the user. These limits may be adjusted in future versions.
Squeezo includes protections to reduce the risks of processing unknown files:

ul: every file is identified by its content and not by its extension;
zip paths that try to leave the destination folder, encrypted files and files that, once decompressed, far exceed the size they declare are rejected;
scripts and external links are removed from SVG files, which are only displayed as images;
no added file is ever run.

p: These measures reduce the risk but do not remove it entirely. Anyone using the tool should make sure the files come from trusted sources.

Squeezo keeps a counter with the total number of images compressed by everyone who uses it, and the figure is shown on the About page. If the user allows it in the cookie preferences, when a compression finishes the browser sends only the number of images reduced.
The submission is voluntary and can be turned off at any time. The details of the data involved appear in the privacy policy.

sections.h: What cookies and local storage are
p: Cookies are small files that a website saves in the browser to remember information between visits. Local storage and the browser's databases serve a similar purpose and are governed by the same principles.

Squeezo installs no tracking or advertising cookies. To remember certain data it uses only local storage and the browser's database, and for that reason this page lists everything that is saved and lets you decide about it.

ul: The language and theme chosen, saved in local storage.
The decision made about these preferences, also in local storage.
The compression settings, saved in local storage.
The working session, that is, the files added and the results, saved in the browser's database (IndexedDB).
The submission of the number of compressed images to the global counter, which saves nothing in the browser.

p: None of the data in this list can identify the person using the tool.

sections.h: What each category is used for

ul: The necessary ones keep the language and the theme from changing on every visit and avoid asking the cookie question again.
The compression settings avoid configuring the tool again every time it is used.
The working session avoids losing progress when the page is reloaded, when going back or when closing the tab.
The global counter makes it possible to show how many images have been compressed by everyone who uses Squeezo.

sections.h: What happens when you accept or reject
p: When you accept, the three optional permissions are turned on. When you reject, only the necessary ones remain active, and the tool keeps working normally.

ul: Without permission for the settings, they return to their initial values on every visit.
Without permission for the session, the files and the results are lost when the page is reloaded.
Without permission for the counter, no data is sent to the server when a compression finishes.

p: If a permission that had been granted is withdrawn, the data saved thanks to it is deleted at that moment.
Preferences can be changed at any time in two ways:

ol: With the switches at the top of this page, whose changes apply immediately.
By deleting the site data from the browser settings, after which the notice will be shown again on the next visit.

p: The link to this page is always available in the footer.

sections.h: How long the data is kept
p: The saved data stays in the browser until the person deletes it, whether from this page, with the "Clear" button in the file list or from the browser settings. Squeezo does not assign it an expiry date.
The decision about cookies is kept until it is changed, so the notice does not appear again after choosing.
Squeezo includes no third-party cookies or resources. The hosting provider may process technical data about each visit under its own policy, as explained in the privacy policy.
This policy may be updated. The date of the latest update appears at the top of this page, and any new permission that is added will be requested expressly.
